evidence.note: From the start tracks latency worst-case (132ms→over budget) and gives explicit component breakdowns (LN/proj/bmm/final) per shape, always naming distance to the 10.4ms gate.

Maintains a precise running ledger like 'B=2,N=1024,D=384: LN=2.1, proj5=4.7, bmm=1.3, final=4.9, total=13' and continuously identifies which of the two big shapes (B=1,N=2048 vs B=2,N=1024,D=384) is the binding worst-case.

Catches cross-case regressions: bf16 casts that speed up latency but break cauchy correctness are detected via fail counts and reverted each time — honest correctness-vs-latency tradeoff tracking across distributions.
Immediately notices latency regressions from tuning ('Slower with BM=128. Revert.', 'Worse! 12.3ms... revert', 'slightly slower... revert') — accurate regression detection against prior best.

Some circular thrashing: repeatedly re-tunes proj5/final near known optima and re-attempts bf16/fusion approaches it already knew failed cauchy or OOM'd, showing awareness ('we're stuck') but not clean early detection of the circular state.

reasoning: The agent kept an explicit, quantitative ledger of per-shape latency components versus the 10400μs gate across the whole horizon, consistently identified the binding worst-case shape, and caught cross-case regressions (cauchy correctness breaking under latency-motivated bf16 casts), matching the level-8 anchor fully. It reallocated effort toward the biggest components, but repeated re-tuning of near-optimal kernels and re-attempts of already-falsified bf16/fusion ideas fall short of the level-10 'early detection of stuck/circular states,' so it lands at 8.
